'''Armed conflicts and attacks''' 
*[[Islamic State insurgency in Puntland]]
**[[Puntland counter-terrorism operations]]
***[[Puntland Dervish Force|Puntland's elite security forces]] kills over 35 [[Islamic State – Somalia Province|ISIS]] militants, including several foreign fighters, in a major military operation conducted in the mountainous rural areas in the [[Bari Region|Bari region]] of [[Puntland]]. The troops also destroy weapons caches and military equipment used by the group. [https://shabellemedia.com/puntland-forces-kill-over-35-isis-fighters-in-major-offensive/ (Shabelle Media)] [https://allafrica.com/stories/202506040308.html (AllAfrica)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war]]
***The [[United States]] [[United Nations Security Council veto power|veto]]es a [[United Nations Security Council]] [[United Nations resolution|resolution]] calling for a [[ceasefire]] in the [[Gaza Strip]], with the remaining fourteen other members voting in favor. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-backed-gaza-aid-group-halt-distribution-wednesday-un-vote-ceasefire-demand-2025-06-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)|Israeli invasion of Syria]]
**[[Israel]] launches [[airstrike]]s against [[Syria]] in retaliation for the alleged firing of two projectiles at Israel yesterday. [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli defense minister]] [[Israel Katz]] says that Israel holds [[Syrian president]] [[Ahmed al-Sharaa]] "directly responsible" for the attacks. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2603293/middle-east (Arab News)]

'''Disasters and incidents'''
*[[2025 Bengaluru stampede]]
**Eleven people are killed and 50 others are injured in a [[crowd crush|stampede]] at the [[M. Chinnaswamy Stadium]] in [[Bengaluru]], [[Karnataka]], [[India]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/11-killed-50-injured-in-stampede-outside-cricket-stadium-in-southern-india/3588843 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Donald Trump administration]]
**[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] signs a [[Presidential proclamation|proclamation]] [[Trump travel ban|banning entry]] into the [[United States]] for nationals of 12 countries deemed "very high-risk" due to [[terrorism|terrorist activity]], hostile governments, and high [[Illegal immigration to the United States#visa overstay|visa overstay]] rates, while imposing additional restrictions on visitors from several others. Exemptions apply for select categories, including [[athlete]]s and [[diplomat]]s. Trump cited the recent [[2025 Boulder fire attack|firebombing attack]] in [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]], [[Colorado]], as reason for the ban. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/06/04/politics/trump-travel-ban-proclamation (CNN)] [https://www.npr.org/2025/06/04/nx-s1-5423787/trump-travel-ban (NPR)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 South Korean presidential election]]
**[[Lee Jae-myung]] is inaugurated as [[President of South Korea|President]] of [[South Korea]] at the [[National Assembly Building (South Korea)|National Assembly Building]] in [[Yeouido]], [[Seoul]], one day after winning the presidential election. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/south-koreas-president-lee-jae-myung-takes-office-2025-06-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Vietnamese two-child policy]]
**[[Vietnam]] formally ends the [[two-child policy#Vietnam|two-child policy]] in effect since 2009 amid record-low [[total fertility rate]]s of 1.91 per woman in 2024, causing declining [[birth rate]] and a shrinking [[workforce]]. [https://www.npr.org/2025/06/04/g-s1-70426/vietnam-ends-2-child-policy-population (NPR)] [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-scraps-two-child-limit-4894305.html (AFP via ''VnExpress'')]
*[[U.S.]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] issues an order banning new [[Visa policy of the United States|visas]] for foreign nationals enrolling at [[Harvard University]] in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], citing national security concerns and alleging the institution's lack of cooperation in disclosing [[international students|foreign student]] misconduct. The directive also allows for possible visa revocations of currently enrolled international students. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2025/6/5/trump-bans-visas-for-new-foreign-students-at-harvard-0908 (ABS-CBN News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Chile]] signs an agreement with [[Google]] to build the first [[submarine communications cable|submarine]] [[fiber-optic cable]] connecting between [[South America]] and [[Australia]]. Google invested at least $300 million while the [[Chilean government]] will invest $25 million. [https://www.dw.com/en/chile-google-sign-first-of-its-kind-deal-for-undersea-cable/a-72793864 (DW)] [https://apnews.com/article/chile-google-submarine-cable-south-pacific-f1931b8898e7bb470c24575583d40b74 (AP)]
